header:
What difference does **$50 more**
a month make on a credit card?
notes: Port case: the content of the live-sheet what-difference-2 sample cut to 3 options. Shows: option times left out (only the first has t 0, so it is already run at frame 1; the kit paces the others: the first at 1.6 s, the next one gap after the previous lane's last landing, squeezed from 2.2 to 1.8 s so it lands before the verdict at 9.0); compound payoffs ("11 yrs 5 mo": the crates are placed by total months, 137 / 52 / 26, and the running counter counts whole years, then pops the exact string); a third metric (Total you pay back) as a grey line under each money value with its label under the money head; deltas; a read of two money values and one of a total; the gold-plate winner. Silent. Maths: $5,000 at 22% APR, 22% ÷ 12 = 1.8333% a month on the balance, a fixed payment, no new charges, simulated month by month (re-checked in Python): first month's interest $91.67 ≈ $92 (so $8, $58, $158 of the first payment comes off the debt). $100/mo: 137 payments = 11 yrs 5 mo, interest $8,678.06, total $13,678.06. $150/mo: 52 payments = 4 yrs 4 mo, interest $2,798.05, total $7,798.05; 8,678.06 − 2,798.05 = $5,880.01 → −$5,880. $250/mo: 26 payments = 2 yrs 2 mo, interest $1,285.72 ≈ $1,286, total $6,285.72 ≈ $6,286; $7,392.34 less → −$7,392. Winner $150: the first $50 a month saves $5,880.
